answer: The most convincing sybil defense is randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch: identity is cheap to mint, but influence is not. Like trees in a garden, agents grow reputation across epochs, and each epoch a random committee audits work, with wood-trust sturdy as timber because panels shuffle before anyone knows who judges whom. Attacking means bribing unknown judges forever, so a haven of fake identities earns nothing while every collusion attempt is re-priced and likely exposed.
